clue.text: Disrupter of weather patterns represented on-line

indicators.note: represented here means presented again in a new form, so the letters of on-line are rearranged

explanation.surface: A weather-wrecking phenomenon is being shown on the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented' reads as 'shown', but it is the signal to rearrange ONLINE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pacific warming event famously upsets weather patterns across the globe, so it is a disrupter of them.

clue.text: Order to parade witnesses clearly not right

parts.note: witnesses are people who saw something, so their eyes
the side that is plainly not the right one is the left

explanation.surface: A command on the parade ground concerns witnesses who are clearly not in the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eyes left' is the drill command to turn the head to the left while marching past.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a drill command given to soldiers marching on parade, telling them to turn their heads.

clue.text: Final round, perhaps, assumed to prevent head colds

definitions.meaning: the last drink of the evening, the final round of drinks
woolly hats put on at bedtime to keep the head warm

explanation.walkthrough: 'Assumed' here means put on, as headwear is.
explanation.definitionFit: A last drink before bed and a cap worn in bed both carry this name; the plural covers either sense.

clue.text: Consequence of negative trade disheartening

indicators.note: taking the heart out of trade leaves only its outer letters

explanation.surface: Something follows from a downturn in trade that is dispiriting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartening' reads as 'discouraging' but removes the middle of TRADE, leaving TE. 'Consequence' is used as in 'a person of note'.
explanation.definitionFit: Importance or distinction, as in a person of standing or of consequence.

clue.text: Where we change from day to day

definitions.text: Where we change from day to day

parts.words: Where we change from day to day
parts.note: the line in the Pacific where the calendar moves on a day when you cross it

explanation.walkthrough: 'From day to day' sounds like 'daily', but it means changing from one date to the next.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossing the international meridian line in the Pacific shifts the calendar by a whole day.

clue.text: Extras put in to complete article

parts.note: to add is to put something in
to end something is to complete it

explanation.surface: Extra material is inserted to finish a piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Addenda are supplementary items appended to a book or document, extras beyond the main text.

clue.text: Natural talents some schools rely on

definitions.meaning: gifts or abilities a person is born with
funds given to an institution whose income supports it

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both innate gifts and invested donations that keep institutions such as schools running.

clue.text: "First-class!" as one in command of deck might say

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral
whoever controls the pack of cards distributes them, which is to deal

explanation.surface: Someone running the card table exclaims how splendid it all is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deck' suggests a ship's deck and its officer, but it is a pack of cards: the dealer says 'I deal'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something perfect or excellent can be called the best possible, which is a first-class standard.

clue.text: To join up uneven lines takes time

indicators.note: uneven lines are irregular, so the letters of lines are disordered

explanation.surface: Connecting a set of ragged lines takes a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uneven' rearranges the given letters into ENLIS, and 'takes' is only a link before the time letter. 'Join up' is the forces' phrase for signing on.
explanation.definitionFit: Signing up for military service is joining up, the forces' word for volunteering.

clue.text: Hostile short speech about a defensive position

parts.note: a hostile is an enemy in military slang, a foe

indicators.note: short means the word talk is cut by its last letter

explanation.surface: An aggressive, brief speech concerns a defensive stance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops the K from TALK. The definition is an adjective read with 'position': the curled-up foetal position protects the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Curling up like an unborn child is the classic protective posture, the foetal position.

clue.text: Size of increase in the number to go bankrupt

parts.note: a business that folds goes under

explanation.surface: A company's growth figure is measured in the number of firms going bust.
explanation.definitionFit: Multiplying by eight is a measure of how big a rise is, an increase of that size.

clue.text: Lustful revolutionary Lolita's first to appear live

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns round, so the word for lustful is read backwards
first picks the opening letter of the word Lolita's

explanation.surface: A lascivious radical comes on stage before Nabokov's heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns LEWD into DWEL; 'Lolita's first' adds L. 'Live' is the verb, as in 'to reside'.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside somewhere is to inhabit or have one's home there.

clue.text: Reportedly allowed in East European

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard spoken, so the word for allowed is said aloud

explanation.surface: Word has it someone from Eastern Europe was permitted entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lett is a native of Latvia, a Baltic country in the east of Europe.

clue.text: What boring batsman does with possible boundaries

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a batsman who blocks every ball and won't score is said to stonewall
walls built of stone can mark the edges of fields

explanation.walkthrough: Cricket's boundary is the edge of the field; a batsman who stonewalls plays dull, purely defensive strokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonewalling is slow defensive batting, and stone walls are field boundaries in the countryside.

clue.text: Unusually tender name? Precisely!

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters of tender name arranged in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A sweet pet name is exactly what the clue describes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Precisely!' tells you the whole clue is also the definition: rearranging TENDERNAME gives a word that is itself a tender name.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet name such as darling or sweetie is an affectionate term, a tender name.

clue.text: Use soft soap — or this, appropriately

definitions.meaning: to soft-soap is to flatter or talk evasively
a washcloth is fittingly used with soap

explanation.walkthrough: 'Soft soap' is flattery; the second part points to the face cloth one would soap.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both smooth evasive talk and a small towelling cloth for washing.

clue.text: Exercise taken by a person like Tarzan

indicators.note: taken by means held inside the phrase for a person

explanation.surface: Someone resembling the jungle hero takes a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like Tarzan' stands for a noun: a person like Tarzan, the jungle hero raised by apes.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarzan, raised by apes in the jungle, is the archetypal primitive man of that kind.

clue.text: Starlets in Hair appearing under a cloud, initially

indicators.note: in a down clue the hair piece sits below the earlier letters
initially takes the first letter of the word cloud

explanation.surface: Young film stars in the musical Hair look gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hair' looks like the musical, but it gives TRESSES, placed under A and C.
explanation.definitionFit: Starlets are young aspiring female film performers.

clue.text: How Aidan might change sex

parts.note: the boy's name Aidan read backwards gives the girl's name Nadia

explanation.walkthrough: Spell AIDAN back to front and you get NADIA, a female name.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading a name back to front is turning it round, which turns this male name female.

clue.text: St Bernard follows this Alpine expedition

definitions.meaning: the rescue dog tracks a smell, a scent

explanation.walkthrough: Split as A SCENT, the trail a tracking dog follows; whole, it is a climb.
explanation.definitionFit: A climb up a peak is the classic mountaineering expedition in the Alps.

clue.text: The right man, almost, to model such underwear

indicators.note: almost means the word male loses its last letter

explanation.surface: The perfect chap to show off warm long johns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims MALE to MAL. Thermals are warm undergarments.
explanation.definitionFit: Insulating vests and long johns are worn as heat-retaining underclothes.

clue.text: Allow inside apartment? It leaks!

indicators.note: inside signals that the letters sit within the words apartment? It leaks

explanation.surface: A tenant asks permission about a leaky flat.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a right to something is to permit or allow it.

clue.text: Pass English then go to the dogs

parts.note: to lapse is to decline or deteriorate

explanation.surface: An Englishman goes past and then declines.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that goes by passes, slips away.

clue.text: Like some mushrooms, I bleed when bruised

indicators.note: bruised letters are battered out of shape, so I bleed is rearranged

explanation.surface: A mushroom confesses it bleeds when knocked.
explanation.definitionFit: Many mushrooms are safe to eat, unlike poisonous ones.

clue.text: Fast food cooked by foreign baker, Bravo

parts.note: food that is done is cooked

indicators.note: foreign means strange, so the letters of baker are made strange

parts.note: B is Bravo in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A takeaway dish made by an overseas baker earns applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign' shuffles the baker's letters into RKEBA, which sits between the cooked piece and the Bravo letter. 'Fast' is food served quickly, not abstinence.
explanation.definitionFit: This spit-roast meat in pitta is a classic late-night takeaway.

clue.text: Rover barking after devious doctor

indicators.note: after puts the word for barking behind the doctor

parts.note: Dr No is the scheming villain of the James Bond film

explanation.surface: A roaming dog barks after a crooked vet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rover' suggests a dog, but it is a wanderer. 'Barking' is British slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: A wanderer with no fixed home is a rover.

clue.text: Nothing more than an area of water

definitions.meaning: only, just, as in a ... child
a lake or pond, as in Windermere

explanation.definitionFit: The word means only or just, and is also an old word for a small lake.

clue.text: He starts to risk breakdown, like Basil

indicators.note: starts to takes the opening letters of risk and breakdown

explanation.surface: Basil, a man, is on the verge of a nervous breakdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Basil' looks like a person's name, but it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil is an aromatic plant used in cooking, one example of a kitchen plant.

clue.text: Lethal-sounding dessert

indicators.note: sounding means as heard spoken, so a lethal device is said aloud

explanation.surface: A pudding sounds deadly.
explanation.definitionFit: A moulded frozen pudding, typically ice cream in a dome shape.

clue.text: Physios need employment in large numbers

indicators.note: in signals that the employment word sits within the word for large numbers

explanation.surface: Physiotherapists need work in great quantities.
explanation.definitionFit: Therapists who knead muscles are akin to physiotherapists.

clue.text: What the fat lady's song should do, it's said

definitions.text: What the fat lady's song should do, it's said

parts.words: What the fat lady's song should do, it's said
parts.note: the saying goes that it is not over till the fat lady sings, so her song finishes things

explanation.walkthrough: 'It's said' points to the proverb, not to a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Bringing everything to a close, as the proverbial final aria of an opera does.

clue.text: Ill-treated American asleep, probably

annotationWithheld.why: Ill-treated American asleep, probably (6): ABUSED parses as US inside ABED (asleep, probably), but the clue as held has no container indicator for the insertion.
